title: Decentralized relaxed-smooth optimization with unrestricted local work and expected sample cost
summary: Dimension-envelope expected sample complexity with heterogeneous local objectives, fresh stochastic gradients, and a known exact communication matrix.

description_paragraphs: Minimize $f(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and have every node return an expected first-order stationary point of this average.
task.formulation: Minimize $f(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x)$ and have every node return an expected first-order stationary point of this average.

description_paragraphs:
For each finite dimension $d$, the continuously differentiable local objectives satisfy $f(x_0)-\inf f\le\Delta$. Only the average must be bounded below. For every node and $\|x-y\|\le1/L_1$, $\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f_i(y)\|\le(L_0+L_1\|
abla f_i(x)\|)\|x-y\|$. Uniform heterogeneity is $\|
abla f_i(x)-
abla f(x)\|\le H$ on the full space.

The known fixed communication matrix $W$ is symmetric, entrywise nonnegative, doubly stochastic, and positive semidefinite, with $0\preceq W\preceq I$ and $\ker(I-W)=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}$. The initial point and all numerical upper bounds are public. The matrix is held fixed in the minimax definition.

description_paragraphs: A local query selects a node $i$ and a point $x\in\mathbb R^d$ and returns $G_i(x;\xi)$ satisfying $\mathbb E[G_i\mid\mathcal F]=\nabla f_i(x)$ and $\mathbb E[\|G_i-\nabla f_i(x)\|^2\mid\mathcal F]\le\sigma^2$ for the complete pre-query history $\mathcal F$. Every call uses fresh randomness. No same-sample second-point reuse or smoothness of random responses is provided. Function values are not returned.

One communication call applies W to any finite stack of local vectors. Exact real local arithmetic is unrestricted and may use the known matrix, signed coefficients, and public randomness. Communication calls are counted separately but are not capped when the total sample count is optimized.

description_paragraphs: $S$ is the total number of local gradient responses over all nodes; every batch response counts. Stopping-time query counts are allowed and the cost is $\sup_I\mathbb E S$. Communication cost $C_{\mathrm{comm}}$ is separate and unconstrained in this projection. For fixed finite dimension let $S_d^*=\inf_A\sup_I\mathbb E S$ subject to the stationarity guarantee; the dimension-envelope quantity is $S^*=\sup_{d\ge1}S_d^*$.

description_paragraphs: Randomized adaptive protocols may select nodes and full-space query points, use stopping-time sample counts, unrestricted exact local computations, and the declared W communication interface. Each output must be locally available.
The expectation includes fresh response randomness and private/public algorithmic randomness. The instance and oracle are fixed before this expectation.

regimes.predicate_text: $m\ge2$, $L_0,L_1,\Delta>0$, $H,\sigma\ge0$, and $0<\varepsilon^2\le c_0\Delta L_H$ for the universal sufficiently small constant in Theorem thm:main; W is any fixed admissible public matrix. The upper bound holds in every finite dimension. The lower bounds choose sufficiently large finite dimension in the constructions of Theorem thm:main, Section 5, and Appendices on the retiring and terminally flat chains. The compared quantity takes sup over finite d; no fixed-dimension minimax assertion is made. For $B_\varepsilon\le A_\varepsilon$, the lower bound strengthens to $\Omega(\mathfrak F_\varepsilon)$ without Xi_epsilon. For $B_\varepsilon>A_\varepsilon$, $N_\varepsilon<2$ and the rate reduces to the coarse fresh-noise scale. An accompanying communication upper bound does not establish a joint sample–communication minimax frontier.
